text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The government is expected to approve the final version of the 1997 state budget draft on November 13.

- One of the top priorities of the government's financial policy for the next few years is a gradual liberalisation of the capital account, aimed at creating conditions for full convertibility of the crown by the year 2000.
- This year's potato harvest is expected to exceed consumption needs by some 170,000 tonnes.
- State guarantees for domestic and foreign loans and bond issues totalled some 60.5 billion crowns between 1990-1995.

NARODNA OBRODA - Jan Smerek, director of steel maker VSZ, said the company would start discussions about possible joint- ventures or joint investment and development strategies with unspecified partners in near future.

- Smerek said one of the two alternatives on how to obtain financial resources to cover the required investments in the steel industry would be the merger of capital of several similar companies to create a stronger entity that would have more leverage in getting loans from banks.

- The second alternative, Smerek said, could be putting together financial sources in several smaller domestic banks to create one stronger financial institution that would be more competitive on the European market.
- Consumption of steel is expected to gradually increase and that the domestic steel producers would be required to start more productive cooperation in near future, Smerek said.
- Investments of up to 100,000 crowns accounted for about 80 percent of the overall direct foreign investment in the first half of this year, totalling some 25 billion crowns.

- The state-run postal monopoly, Slovenska Posta s.p., will increase prices of its services by an average of one-third from the beginning of next year. The price hike should bring about 400 million crowns in extra revenues.
- Investment fund Sovensky Strojarensky Fond, created by the heavy-engineering company ZTS TEES Martin for the first wave of privatisation, will go into liquidation.
- Hewlett-Packard ranks first in personal computer sales in Slovakia in the first half of this year, and accounted for some 13 percent of the local market.

- Engineering company Povazske Strojarne will start production of DV-2 jet engines within two years, after eight years of development and tests with investments of around $600 million. The company said Russia was interested in buying about 800 engines a year, and up to 1,200 engines could be sold in western Europe.

SLOVENSKA REPUBLIKA - Slovakia is expected to temporarily abolish custom duties on grain imports to cover the current shortage of fodder cereals. The abolition is expected to last until the end of July 1997.
